patients.summary: Retired physics professor who joined in 2017 with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, CKD 3a and left hip arthritis. Mild cognitive impairment in 2020, a resected mucin-producing pancreatic adenocarcinoma with transient DIC in 2023, flash pulmonary edema and an anterior STEMI in 2024, E. coli septic shock he survived in 2025, and a right MCA stroke in April 2026 after his last practice visit.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
66 y/o man transferring care; his longtime internist retired this summer. Brought a shopping bag of bottles, which made reconciliation easy.

HTN since about 2006, lisinopril 10 for years, does not check at home. T2DM about 7 years, metformin 1000 BID, says last A1c was 'in the sixes'. Told a few years ago his kidney numbers were 'a little low' - CKD stage 3a per his account, no nephrology. L hip arthritis, aches after long walks, takes acetaminophen a few times a week, avoids ibuprofen because of an ulcer in the 1990s (treated, scoped back then, no bleeding since). Stays on omeprazole because he takes aspirin. Atorvastatin 40 and aspirin started by old doctor 'because of the diabetes'.

PSH: appendix out at 24, open incision.
FHx: father MI at 71. Mother T2DM, stroke at 76. Paternal uncle pancreatic cancer.
SHx: married, lives with wife in Florence. Daughter nearby, son lives in Germany. Retired university physics professor (PhD). Former smoker, about 20 pack-years, quit roughly 15 years ago. Alcohol a drink or two a month. Walks most days.
Allergies: NKDA.

ROS negative in detail apart from the hip.

Exam: BP and pulse as recorded. Pleasant, articulate, good historian. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyromegaly, no bruits. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed RLQ scar. Ext without edema; L hip internal rotation a bit limited and uncomfortable at end range. Feet: skin intact, monofilament intact bilaterally, DP pulses 2+.

A/P
1. HTN - at goal on lisinopril 10. Continue.
2. T2DM - metformin 1000 BID. A1c, UACR today. Eye exam due - he has an optometrist.
3. CKD 3a - BMP today to set our own baseline. Keep NSAIDs off the table.
4. L hip OA - acetaminophen PRN, keep walking.
5. Remote PUD on aspirin - continue omeprazole.
6. Lipids/ASA - continue atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81.
7. HM - one-time HCV and HIV today. Will request old records for colonoscopy and vaccines. Former smoker age 65-75: AAA screening ultrasound ordered. Flu shot at nurse visit next month.

RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Office Visit - Memory
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Visit requested by his wife, who came with him. Over roughly the last year he has missed a dentist appointment and a lunch with a former colleague, keeps losing his reading glasses and keys, and asks her the same question twice within an hour. He acknowledges the appointments but thinks the rest is ordinary aging. No getting lost, no trouble finding words, no change in personality, no hallucinations. Still manages his pills with a pillbox and pays the bills; she now double-checks the calendar.
No head injury, no new meds, mood fine, sleeping well, alcohol minimal.
Exam: BP at goal. Alert, oriented, conversational and engaged. Recalled 1 of 3 words at 5 minutes; clock drawing correct. Gait normal. No focal neuro findings.
A/P: Subjective and observed memory decline over a year in a 68 y/o with vascular risk factors. Labs at his last draw unremarkable. Referring to neurology for formal cognitive testing; they will likely want B12/TSH, which can be done there. BMP today. Discussed that a name for this, if there is one, is the neurologist's call.

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY - CONSULTATION LETTER
Date of visit: 04/21/2020
Referred by primary care for memory complaints.

Thank you for referring Mr. Gallo, a 68-year-old retired physics professor, seen with his wife. For about a year he has struggled to keep track of appointments and has been misplacing everyday objects more often. His wife reports that he will ask the same question again during a single conversation. Neither of them describes problems with language, with spatial tasks or navigation, or any change in his personality or behavior.

Background: hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both under good control on lisinopril and metformin; CKD stage 3a; left hip osteoarthritis; remote peptic ulcer. Appendectomy at 24. Also takes omeprazole, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, acetaminophen as needed. NKDA.
Family history: father MI at 71; mother type 2 diabetes and a stroke at 76; paternal uncle with pancreatic cancer.
Social: married; holds a master's and a doctorate in physics; former smoker (quit about 18 years ago, 20 pack-years); rare alcohol.

Examination: Awake, alert, oriented to person, place and time. Mini-Mental State Examination 28/30, both points lost on delayed recall. Montreal Cognitive Assessment 23/30, losing points on delayed recall, attention and executive items (trails, fluency). Cranial nerves, motor, sensory, coordination and gait unremarkable.

Laboratory (drawn today): fasting glucose 98 mg/dL; HbA1c 6.2%; vitamin B12 450 pg/mL; TSH 2.5 mIU/L. No reversible metabolic contributor identified.

Impression: Mild cognitive impairment, predominantly amnestic with some attention and executive involvement. Independent in daily function.

Plan:
1. Start donepezil 5 mg nightly; if tolerated after four weeks, increase to 10 mg nightly. Common side effects (vivid dreams, loose stools, nausea) reviewed.
2. Aerobic exercise, continued intellectual and social engagement, good sleep.
3. Continue vascular risk factor control with primary care.
4. Neurology follow-up in about 18 months, sooner for any change.

Allergies: NKDA.
Outside neurology

documents.title: Orthopedic Consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ORTHOPEDICS - OFFICE CONSULTATION
Date of service: 10/14/2020

History: 69-year-old man seen by neurology this spring for memory concerns, with known left hip osteoarthritis, referred for six months of increasing left hip pain. Rising from a chair and climbing stairs are now difficult. Pain accumulates across the day with use and is relieved by resting. Morning stiffness lasts only a few minutes. He reports no swelling of the joint and no fevers, chills or weight change.
PMH: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, CKD 3a, mild cognitive impairment, remote peptic ulcer. PSH: appendectomy.
Medications: lisinopril, metformin, omeprazole, donepezil 10 mg, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, acetaminophen 500 mg as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 18 years ago; rare alcohol; retired university physics professor.
Family history noncontributory to this complaint.

Examination: Left hip with reduced range of motion in all planes and moderate crepitus on passive motion. No effusion, no warmth. Distal neurovascular status intact.

Assessment: Symptomatic left hip osteoarthritis.
Plan: Conservative management. Continue acetaminophen as needed; NSAIDs avoided given his kidney function and ulcer history. Home exercise program for hip strength and range of motion, handout given. Follow up as needed if function declines further.
Outside orthopedics

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY - FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Date of visit: 10/25/2021

Mr. Gallo returned for scheduled follow-up roughly a year and a half after his first visit, accompanied this time by his daughter, who gave additional history. Her main worry is driving: he has been involved in two minor collisions over the past year and has had trouble navigating to places he knows well. She asked what the next step should be.

Interval history: type 2 diabetes, hypertension (well controlled) and mild cognitive impairment diagnosed at his first visit. Medications include donepezil 10 mg nightly, metformin, lisinopril, omeprazole, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg and acetaminophen as needed. NKDA. Former smoker, rare alcohol, retired physics professor.

Vital signs: BP 132/78 mmHg, HR 78.
Examination: Alert and oriented x3. Corrected visual acuity 20/30 in each eye. MMSE 24/30, with errors on attention (serial sevens) and recall. Remainder of neurological exam nonfocal.

Impression: Mild cognitive impairment, with a decline in MMSE from 28 to 24 since April 2020 and new concerns about driving safety.

Plan:
1. Formal driving evaluation through an occupational therapy driver rehabilitation program is recommended; information given to his daughter. Until it is completed we advised he limit driving to short familiar daytime trips, or not drive.
2. Continue donepezil 10 mg nightly.
3. Continue exercise and cognitive and social engagement.
4. Return in 12 months or sooner with changes.
Outside neurology

documents.title: Office Visit - Jaundice
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Wife called yesterday for a same-day slot; they had canceled the March visit because he 'felt run down'. Seen first thing.
Three months of steadily increasing fatigue. Has lost about 10 kg - scale today confirms, 76 kg vs 86 in December. Urine dark like tea for a few weeks; over the past week his wife noticed his eyes and then his skin turning yellow. He denies abdominal pain. No fever, no vomiting, no new meds, no alcohol beyond his usual rare drink.
Exam: thin compared with his baseline, clearly icteric sclerae and jaundiced skin. Afebrile. Abdomen soft, nontender; a smooth rounded fullness under the right costal margin. No ascites. No asterixis.
A: Painless jaundice with weight loss in a 71 y/o - obstructive process until proven otherwise; pancreatic or biliary malignancy high on the list. Family history of pancreatic cancer (paternal uncle).
P: Called GI directly - they will see him Friday 4/21 with labs and ultrasound the same day. Discussed honestly with him and his wife what we are looking for. Return precautions for fever, pain, confusion. I'll call after GI.

reports.text: Indication: jaundice. Liver normal in size and echotexture without focal lesion. Intrahepatic biliary ducts dilated. Common bile duct dilated. Gallbladder distended, no gallstones, no wall thickening, no pericholecystic fluid. Pancreatic head partially obscured by bowel gas. Kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. Spleen normal. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Intra- and extrahepatic biliary dilation without gallstones; distended gallbladder. Cross-sectional imaging recommended.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 04/21/2023
Urgent referral from primary care.

HPI: 71-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment and left hip osteoarthritis presenting with new symptoms: progressive fatigue for three months, a 10 kg weight loss and dark urine. No abdominal pain. He and his wife have noticed yellowing of his skin and eyes.
PMH: hypertension (lisinopril), type 2 diabetes (metformin), CKD 3a, remote peptic ulcer disease, MCI. PSH: appendectomy.
Medications: lisinopril 10 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg daily, donepezil 10 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, acetaminophen 500 mg PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: paternal uncle with pancreatic adenocarcinoma; father MI at 71; mother diabetes and stroke at 76.
Social: former smoker (20 pack-years, quit 18 years ago), rare alcohol, retired physics professor.

Exam: Cachectic and jaundiced. Abdomen soft, nontender; the gallbladder is palpable and distended.

Labs today: total bilirubin 5.2 mg/dL (0.3-1.2), direct bilirubin 3.8 mg/dL (0.0-0.3), alkaline phosphatase 420 U/L (40-130), AST 80 U/L (10-40), ALT 75 U/L (7-56).
Abdominal ultrasound today: dilated intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts, no gallstones.

Impression: Painless obstructive jaundice with a Courvoisier gallbladder and weight loss; malignant distal biliary obstruction suspected.
Plan: CT abdomen with pancreatic protocol Monday. If a mass is confirmed, ERCP with biliary stent and EUS-guided tissue sampling next week. Will keep primary care informed.
Outside gastroenterology

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Indication: obstructive jaundice. Technique: pancreatic protocol, arterial and portal venous phases. Findings: Hypoattenuating mass in the pancreatic head measuring 2.7 x 2.4 cm in axial dimensions. Upstream pancreatic duct mildly dilated. Intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts dilated to the level of the pancreatic head; distended gallbladder without stones. Fat planes about the superior mesenteric artery, celiac axis and portal-superior mesenteric vein confluence preserved. Liver without focal lesion. No ascites. No enlarged lymph nodes. Adrenals, kidneys and spleen unremarkable. Lung bases clear. Colon and small bowel unremarkable. Healed appendectomy.
reports.conclusion: Pancreatic head mass with biliary and pancreatic ductal dilation, no vascular involvement and no evidence of metastatic disease. Findings suspicious for pancreatic adenocarcinoma; tissue sampling recommended.

OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - PROCEDURE REPORT
Date of procedure: 05/02/2023
Procedures: endoscopic ultrasound with fine-needle biopsy; ERCP with biliary stent placement.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care.
EUS: 2.6 cm hypoechoic mass in the pancreatic head abutting the distal common bile duct; no vascular invasion; no suspicious nodes seen. Three passes with a 22-gauge biopsy needle; on-site evaluation adequate.
ERCP: distal common bile duct stricture; biliary sphincterotomy and placement of a 10 Fr plastic biliary stent with good drainage of bile.
Pre-procedure coagulation: platelets 112 K/uL, PT 15.1 s, INR 1.3, fibrinogen 138 mg/dL, D-dimer 4.6 mcg/mL FEU. No bleeding with sphincterotomy.
Complications: none.
Pathology (05/05): adenocarcinoma, mucin-producing.
Impression: Mucin-producing pancreatic adenocarcinoma of the head, locally resectable by imaging, with laboratory evidence of chronic low-grade disseminated intravascular coagulation.
Plan: referral to surgical oncology placed. Primary care notified.
Allergies: NKDA.

OUTSIDE SURGICAL ONCOLOGY - CONSULTATION

71-year-old man with a 2.6-2.7 cm mucin-producing adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head presenting with painless jaundice, now stented. Coagulation studies at diagnosis consistent with chronic low-grade DIC, no bleeding or thrombosis.

Imaging reviewed at tumor board: no arterial or venous involvement, no distant disease - resectable.

Recommendation: pancreaticoduodenectomy, followed by adjuvant chemotherapy with medical oncology. Risks including leak, delayed gastric emptying, infection, bleeding, worsening diabetes and death discussed with patient, wife and daughter; they wish to proceed. Surgery scheduled 06/07/2023. Preoperative evaluation and anesthesia review arranged.

documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - CARDIOLOGY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 10/17/2024 via the emergency department; discharged 10/20/2024.

Presentation: 73-year-old man, six months after an admission for flash pulmonary edema, brought in with crushing chest pain radiating to the left shoulder. ECG: ST elevation V1-V3. STEMI alert activated.
Catheterization 10/17: acute occlusion of the proximal left anterior descending artery, treated with a single drug-eluting stent with TIMI 3 flow restored. Other vessels without flow-limiting disease. Right radial access.
CK-MB before PCI 9.4 ng/mL, rising to 81 ng/mL after reperfusion; interpreted as myocardial reperfusion injury. No arrhythmia on telemetry.
Echo 10/18: LVEF about 50%, mild anteroseptal hypokinesis.
Diagnoses: acute anterior STEMI treated with PCI/DES to the proximal LAD; myocardial reperfusion injury.
Other history: resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma (2023, mucin-producing, with chronic DIC at diagnosis), hypertension, type 2 diabetes, CKD 3a, mild cognitive impairment, hip osteoarthritis, remote PUD.
Discharge medications: aspirin 81 mg daily; clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 12 months - do not stop without cardiology; metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily (new); atorvastatin 40 mg daily; lisinopril 10 mg daily; metformin 1000 mg BID; omeprazole 20 mg daily; donepezil 10 mg nightly; acetaminophen PRN; furosemide 20 mg daily.

Follow-up: cardiology in 6 weeks; primary care within 1 week.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Septic Shock
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 04/28/2025 through the ED to the ICU; transferred to the medical floor 05/03; discharged home 05/09/2025.

Presenting history: 73-year-old man with resected mucin-producing pancreatic adenocarcinoma, mild cognitive impairment and a recent anterior STEMI with LAD stent (10/2024) and flash pulmonary edema (04/2024), with 18 hours of worsening abdominal pain, fever and chills. Per his wife he had two days of tiredness and poor appetite; rigors and the sharper pain began abruptly the morning of admission. His daughter had noticed he was more withdrawn and eating less than usual. Travel history noncontributory.

On arrival: T 39.4 C, HR 128, RR 28, BP 84/52. Acutely ill, diaphoretic and intermittently confused; warm skin with bounding pulses suggesting distributive shock. Abdomen diffusely tender without rebound or guarding; hypoactive bowel sounds.
Labs: WBC 21.8 K/uL with 89% neutrophils and left shift; lactate 4.7 mmol/L; procalcitonin 18.4 ng/mL; creatinine rising to 2.74 mg/dL on day 2; AST 318 / ALT 266 U/L on day 2, consistent with hypoperfusion. Blood cultures: gram-negative rods in 2 of 2 sets, E. coli.
Imaging: CXR low volumes with bibasilar atelectasis. Echo hyperdynamic LV with preserved function, cardiogenic shock unlikely. CT abdomen/pelvis: diffuse bowel wall thickening concerning for ischemia and bacterial translocation, no free air or abscess.

Course: IV fluids and piperacillin-tazobactam started in the ED. Hypotension persisted despite fluids over the first 12 hours, requiring norepinephrine and ICU transfer. On day 2 his confusion worsened, hands and feet became mottled and urine output fell; he was intubated for worsening mental status and respiratory distress. Surgery consulted: no operative indication, bowel rest. He then turned the corner - norepinephrine weaned off and extubated on day 4, ICU for 5 days total. His son flew in from Germany during the ICU stay. Repeat CT 05/03: bowel wall thickening resolving. Diet advanced. Delirium cleared by discharge; family feels he is near his pre-illness baseline.
AKI resolved toward baseline: creatinine 1.62 mg/dL at discharge.

Discharge diagnoses: septic shock due to E. coli bacteremia; bowel wall thickening concerning for ischemia, resolving with nonoperative care; acute kidney injury; ischemic hepatitis, resolving.
Discharge medications: ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily to complete 14 days of antibiotics; aspirin 81 mg; clopidogrel 75 mg; metoprolol succinate 25 mg; atorvastatin 40 mg; metformin 1000 mg BID (resumed at discharge with creatinine 1.62); omeprazole 20 mg; donepezil 10 mg; acetaminophen PRN. HOLD lisinopril until primary care rechecks kidney function. Furosemide STOPPED.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: primary care within 1 week with BMP.
Regional hospital

documents.body: Dilated eye exam 08/11/2025 (first in two years; missed during illness). VA cc 20/30 OU. Anterior segments unremarkable. No diabetic retinopathy OU. Recheck 12 months.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV with wife. Hard year - heart attack last fall, ICU in the spring - and he is back to daily walks and reading.
Function: ADLs independent with reminders; wife manages IADLs and medications (blister packs from pharmacy). Cane outdoors. No falls. PHQ-2 1. Hearing fine.
Cognition: wife notes no new decline since recovering from the hospitalization. Donepezil continues. Neurology not seen since 2021; they decline a new referral for now.
Eye exam August: no retinopathy.
ACP revisited: wishes as documented in 2023; proxy wife, alternate daughter.
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Feet: monofilament intact.
Plan: labs; high-dose flu and updated COVID today. Oncology CT due in October; cardiology October.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your wellness labs look good: blood count normal, kidney function stable, cholesterol on target, no protein in the urine.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY - OFFICE NOTE
Date of visit: 10/21/2025
One year after anterior STEMI with proximal LAD DES. Interval septic shock admission in April-May, recovered. No angina, no dyspnea, no bleeding on dual antiplatelet therapy.
Medications reviewed: aspirin 81 mg, clopidogrel 75 mg, metoprolol succinate 25 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, metformin, omeprazole, donepezil.
Exam: BP and heart rate at goal; lungs clear; no edema.
Plan: 12 months of DAPT complete - stop clopidogrel today. Continue aspirin 81 mg indefinitely, metoprolol succinate, atorvastatin, lisinopril. Return in one year.
Outside cardiology

documents.title: Scan and heart doctor update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Writing for Russell. His cancer scan in October was clear, the oncologist told us in person - next scan in the spring. The cardiologist stopped the clopidogrel, so he's down one pill. Thought you would want to know. - his wife

documents.title: RE: Scan and heart doctor update
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thank you - great news on both. We have the cardiology note. We don't have the oncology note yet and have requested it.

documents.title: Records request - oncology
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed request to the oncology office for the October 2025 surveillance visit note and CT report.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing well. Cardiology stopped clopidogrel in October after 12 months - list updated; aspirin continues with omeprazole. Oncology note from October still not received; per wife, CT clear.
No chest pain, no breathlessness, eating well. September labs in his usual range.
Exam: BP at goal. Heart regular, lungs clear. No edema.
Plan: A1c today. Continue lisinopril, metformin, metoprolol, atorvastatin, aspirin, omeprazole, donepezil, acetaminophen PRN. Visit in March.

documents.title: Renewal requests
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy (blister-pack service) requested renewals: lisinopril 10, metformin 1000, metoprolol succinate 25, atorvastatin 40, omeprazole 20, donepezil 10, aspirin 81. Renewed x 90 days with 3 refills per PCP. Clopidogrel removed from their profile at our request.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine visit with wife. Quiet winter. No chest pain, dyspnea, edema, fevers or abdominal symptoms. Walks indoors at the mall on cold days. December A1c 7.3, acceptable for him.
Oncology next CT due this spring - they will schedule.
Exam: BP at goal. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Gait steady with cane.
A/P: HTN, T2DM, CKD 3a, CAD s/p LAD stent, resected pancreatic cancer under surveillance, MCI, L hip OA - all stable. BMP, CBC, A1c today. No changes. Return in about 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Friday's labs: kidney function and potassium are right where they usually sit for you, blood count normal, A1c fine for your goal. Nothing to change. See you in the late summer.

reports.text: No intracranial hemorrhage. No mass effect or midline shift. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age. No extra-axial collection. Calvarium intact.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 04/23/2026

CC: sudden difficulty eating, bumping into things on the left.
HPI: 74-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes, a resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma and septic shock last spring, brought in by his daughter. At breakfast this morning she saw him struggling to eat, knocking into objects on his left side, and apparently unaware of his left arm.
Home meds (per pharmacy list): lisinopril 10 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg, donepezil 10 mg, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, metoprolol succinate 25 mg, acetaminophen PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
Vitals: BP 150/90, HR 78, RR 16.
Neuro exam: does not respond to visual stimuli on the left; left-sided weakness; reading a sentence, he reads only its right half; speech fluent; appears unaware of his deficits.
CT head non-contrast: no acute hemorrhage.
Impression: acute right middle cerebral artery territory stroke.
Disposition: stroke team at bedside; admitted to the stroke service for further evaluation and management.
Regional hospital emergency department

documents.title: Dad is in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is Russell's daughter, writing from his account with Mom's permission. Dad had a stroke on Thursday morning - I took him to the ER when he couldn't manage his breakfast and kept missing things on his left. He's still in the hospital on the stroke unit. We'll let you know when he's coming home. Please let his doctor know.

documents.title: RE: Dad is in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling us, and I'm so sorry. Please ask the hospital team to send us his discharge summary, and let us know when he is home so we can see him. Thinking of all of you.

documents.title: Refill request - metformin
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy requested an early refill of metformin 1000 mg for the blister-pack cycle. Last renewal 1/20. Approved per PCP. Hospital discharge summary still not received - re-requested.

documents.title: Follow-up appointment for Dad
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, it's Russell's daughter again. Dad has been home with us for a while now and is doing his therapy. We'd like to get him in to see his regular doctor. Mornings are best. We'll bring his hospital paperwork.

documents.title: RE: Follow-up appointment for Dad
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi - we've booked him with his physician on Tuesday 9/1 at 9:30, a longer appointment. Please bring the hospital paperwork and all his current medications.
